find: Landon presents belonging as something that can stretch across distance. Even as Cook sailed to the other side of the world, the idea of home and family remained a <dfn class="term" data-def="A fixed point to which something is attached, providing stability; metaphorically, something that keeps a person grounded.">anchor</dfn>. The poem uses the natural imagery of the sea and sky to evoke both freedom and longing. For Landon, nature is the medium through which separated people remain connected — they look at the same sky, are carried by the same wind.
replace: Landon presents belonging as something built in play and then lost. The children turn the garden pond into the South Seas and the water lilies into islands, and that shared game becomes an <dfn class="term" data-def="A fixed point to which something is attached, providing stability; metaphorically, something that keeps a person grounded.">anchor</dfn> for the memory. The poem borrows sea and sky imagery to evoke adventure and longing. By the end the garden has been ploughed up and the closeness with her brother has faded, so nature marks the loss as well as the joy.
note: F1: the siblings are never apart; the poem's loss is time, not distance.
